text:
Boston beat San Jose 6-3, but the chances were close to even, and the gap came from the net. At even strength the expected goals were BOS 2.21, SJS 2.24, and the simulated replays gave Boston only a 53 percent claim on the win. SJS had 65 shot attempts to 50 and put 38 on goal to BOS's 26, yet Yaroslav Askarov faced 25 shots and allowed five, 1.68 goals worse than expected.

Fraser Minten opened the scoring at 12:55 of the first, and Jacob Trouba tied it 2:34 later on a slap shot that had a 1 percent chance of going in. Charlie McAvoy restored the lead before the period ended. Macklin Celebrini and Ivar Stenberg answered with power-play goals in the second and third, Stenberg's tying it at 2-2 and Celebrini's making it 4-3, but each time Boston had a reply. Matthew Poitras tipped one in to make it 3-2, and Pavel Zacha scored at 19:57 of the second for a 4-2 lead.

The third period belonged to Minten, who tipped in his second at 11:47 to make it 5-3, and Will Borgen sealed it at 18:18. Jeremy Swayman stopped 35 of 38, saving 0.15 goals above expectation, which was enough. SJS scored on two of four power plays, but Boston's 19 blocked shots to 9 helped hold the shots to a lower quality than their volume suggested.
